name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+40 partisan lean makes a Democratic win overwhelming
Chris Rabb has dominant fundraising and outside support versus a lightly funded independent
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot, but the seat stays in the same party's column
No polls or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals and markets
model.rationale: The D+40 fundamentals make this seat effectively unwinnable for the opposition, and Rabb's roughly $1.3 million raised plus $1.6 million in outside support dwarfs Mahoney's $10,800. Markets price the Democratic side near 97%, consistent with a Safe D call.
model.watch: A surprise independent surge or an unexpected third-party dynamic is the only plausible path to narrowing this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Philadelphia's 3rd District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean around D+40. Dwight Evans is retiring, leaving an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Chris Rabb faces only Dennis Mahoney, an independent with minimal funding. Rabb has raised about $1.3 million and benefits from roughly $1.6 million in outside support, while Mahoney has raised under $11,000 with no outside spending.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side near 97%, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no polls available, the forecast leans on the district's overwhelming fundamentals, pointing to a Safe Democratic hold with a margin in the low thirties.
